stem: Find the area of this triangle. The first steps are done. Finish it.
figure:
<svg viewBox="0 0 170 92" width="100%" style="max-width:170px;display:block;margin:.4rem 0" font-family="-apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" aria-label="A triangle with base 10 cm and a height of 6 cm marked at a right angle">
        <polygon points="15,72 155,72 95,10" fill="#e6f4ec" stroke="#1d1d1b" stroke-width="2"/>
        <line x1="95" y1="10" x2="95" y2="72" stroke="#2b5797" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/>
        <rect x="95" y="64" width="8" height="8" fill="none" stroke="#2b5797"/>
        <text x="85" y="88" text-anchor="middle" fill="#1d1d1b">10 cm</text>
        <text x="101" y="44" fill="#2b5797">6 cm</text>
      </svg>

misconceptions.message: You did base × height. A triangle is half of that.
You halved the base and stopped. Multiply by the height as well.

stem: A 12 cm by 8 cm rectangle has a 4 cm by 3 cm corner cut out. Find the area left. The first step is done. Finish it.
figure:
<svg viewBox="0 0 190 110" width="100%" style="max-width:190px;display:block;margin:.4rem 0" font-family="-apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" aria-label="A 12 cm by 8 cm rectangle with a 4 cm by 3 cm rectangle removed from the top right corner">
        <polygon points="15,18 135,18 135,48 175,48 175,98 15,98" fill="#e6f4ec" stroke="#1d1d1b" stroke-width="2"/>
        <rect x="135" y="18" width="40" height="30" fill="none" stroke="#c8372d" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/>
        <text x="155" y="14" text-anchor="middle" fill="#c8372d">4</text>
        <text x="181" y="36" fill="#c8372d">3</text>
        <text x="95" y="110" text-anchor="middle" fill="#1d1d1b">12 cm</text>
        <text x="11" y="60" text-anchor="end" fill="#1d1d1b">8 cm</text>
      </svg>
hint: Work out the area of the corner piece next.
working: Big rectangle: 12 × 8 = 96 cm². Corner piece: 4 × 3 = 12 cm². Left: 96 − 12 = 84 cm².

misconceptions.message: That is the whole rectangle. The corner piece still has to come off.
That is the piece cut out, not the shape left.
You added the corner piece instead of taking it off.

stem: Find the area of this trapezium.
figure:
<svg viewBox="0 0 190 96" width="100%" style="max-width:190px;display:block;margin:.4rem 0" font-family="-apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" aria-label="A trapezium with parallel sides 5 cm on top and 9 cm at the bottom, and height 6 cm">
        <polygon points="60,16 130,16 165,76 25,76" fill="#e6f4ec" stroke="#1d1d1b" stroke-width="2"/>
        <line x1="95" y1="16" x2="95" y2="76" stroke="#2b5797" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/>
        <rect x="95" y="68" width="8" height="8" fill="none" stroke="#2b5797"/>
        <text x="95" y="12" text-anchor="middle" fill="#1d1d1b">5 cm</text>
        <text x="95" y="92" text-anchor="middle" fill="#1d1d1b">9 cm</text>
        <text x="101" y="48" fill="#2b5797">6 cm</text>
      </svg>
hint: Add the two parallel sides first: 5 + 9.

misconceptions.message: You forgot the half. Multiply by ½ at the end.
You multiplied 5 by 9. Add the parallel sides first.
You used 5 and 9 as base and height of a triangle. This is a trapezium.

stem: Find the area of this circle. Give your answer in terms of pi, like 9pi.
figure:
<svg viewBox="0 0 120 120" width="100%" style="max-width:120px;display:block;margin:.4rem 0" font-family="-apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" aria-label="A circle with a radius of 5 cm marked from the centre to the edge">
        <circle cx="60" cy="60" r="48" fill="#e6f4ec" stroke="#1d1d1b" stroke-width="2"/>
        <line x1="60" y1="60" x2="108" y2="60" stroke="#2b5797" stroke-width="2"/>
        <circle cx="60" cy="60" r="2.5" fill="#1d1d1b"/>
        <text x="84" y="54" text-anchor="middle" fill="#2b5797">5 cm</text>
      </svg>
hint: This is not a compound shape. The area of a circle is pi × r × r.
working: A circle needs its own formula: area = pi × r². Here r = 5, so 5² = 25 and the area is 25pi cm².

misconceptions.message: That is the distance round the edge, 2 × pi × r. Area squares the radius.
You used the diameter, 10. The formula uses the radius.
You dropped the pi. The question asks for the area in terms of pi.

stem: A lawn is 8 m by 5 m, with a 2 m by 2 m patio in one corner. Turf costs £3 for each square metre. How much does turfing the rest cost, in pounds?
figure:
<svg viewBox="0 0 190 116" width="100%" style="max-width:190px;display:block;margin:.4rem 0" font-family="-apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" aria-label="An 8 m by 5 m rectangle with a 2 m by 2 m square patio in the bottom right corner">
        <rect x="15" y="16" width="160" height="80" fill="#e6f4ec" stroke="#1d1d1b" stroke-width="2"/>
        <rect x="135" y="64" width="40" height="32" fill="#efeeea" stroke="#5f5f5a"/>
        <text x="155" y="84" text-anchor="middle" fill="#5f5f5a">patio</text>
        <text x="95" y="112" text-anchor="middle" fill="#1d1d1b">8 m</text>
        <text x="11" y="60" text-anchor="end" fill="#1d1d1b">5 m</text>
        <text x="155" y="60" text-anchor="middle" fill="#5f5f5a">2 by 2</text>
      </svg>
hint: Find the turfed area first, in square metres.
working: Whole lawn: 8 × 5 = 40 m². Patio: 2 × 2 = 4 m². Turfed: 40 − 4 = 36 m². Cost: 36 × 3 = £108.

misconceptions.message: You used the whole 8 by 5 lawn. The patio corner is not turfed.
That is the area in square metres. The question asks for the cost.
You found the cost of the patio corner, not the lawn.
